Assuming you mean **Z.ai’s flagship GLM‑5.3**, it is a **753B-parameter, decoder-only sparse Mixture-of-Experts Transformer**, with roughly **40B parameters activated per token**. Despite the “5.3” label, its pretrained architecture is unchanged from GLM‑5.2; the improvements come from additional post-training.[1][2][3]

## Architecture

| Component | Specification |
|---|---|
| Model class | `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` [4] |
| Decoder layers | 78 [3][4] |
| Hidden width | 6,144 [4] |
| Attention heads | 64 [4] |
| Parameters | 753B total, approximately 40B active/token [2][3] |
| Feed-forward layers | 3 dense MLP layers, followed by 75 MoE layers [3] |
| MoE routing | 256 routed experts/layer; top 8 selected per token; 1 shared expert [3][4] |
| Dense MLP width | 12,288 [4] |
| Expert MLP width | 2,048 [4] |
| Context window | 1,048,576 tokens [1][4] |
| Vocabulary | 154,880 tokens [4] |
| Output limit | 128K tokens through Z.ai’s API [1] |
| Modality | Text input and output [1][3] |
| Drafting | One multi-token-prediction layer [3][4] |

## Data path

```text
Tokens
  ↓
Embedding: 154,880 vocabulary → 6,144 hidden dimensions
  ↓
3 × [Sparse latent attention → Dense MLP]
  ↓
75 × [Sparse latent attention → MoE]
       ├─ 256 routed experts
       ├─ Top 8 activated for each token
       └─ 1 shared expert
  ↓
Final RMSNorm
  ↓
Untied language-model head
  ↓
Next-token probabilities

Auxiliary MTP layer → speculative draft tokens → main-model verification
```

## Sparse attention

GLM‑5.3 combines **Multi-head Latent Attention** with **DeepSeek Sparse Attention**. The latent representation compresses keys and values—its configuration uses a 512-dimensional KV low-rank space—while a learned DSA indexer selects only **2,048 historical positions per query**, rather than attending densely over the entire million-token history.[3][4]

Its **IndexShare** mechanism periodically computes a full attention index and reuses it across groups of four layers. Z.ai reports that this cuts per-token computation by 2.9 times at one-million-token context compared with running separate indexing throughout the stack.[4][5]

## What changed in 5.3?

The architecture itself did not materially change from GLM‑5.2. Z.ai concentrated on reinforcement-learning post-training with larger numbers of executable, verifiable, long-horizon environments—particularly complex software-engineering and agent tasks.[2][1]

Reasoning is always enabled at the API level. Users can select `low`, `high`, or `max` reasoning effort, with `max` as the default; reasoning cannot be disabled as it could in some earlier integrations.[1]

## Not the Flash model

**GLM‑5.3‑Flash is architecturally different.** It is a separately pretrained, natively multimodal model with 320B total and 18B active parameters, using 45 decoder layers: 34 Kimi Delta Attention layers and 11 KPool-DSA layers, plus four-stream manifold-constrained hyper-connections.[6][7]

| Feature | GLM‑5.3 | GLM‑5.3‑Flash |
|---|---:|---:|
| Total/active parameters | 753B / ~40B [3] | 320B / 18B [7] |
| Layers | 78 [3] | 45 [7] |
| Attention | MLA + DSA | KDA linear attention + KPool-DSA [7] |
| Routed experts | 256, top-8 [3] | 288, top-8 [7] |
| Modality | Text-only [1] | Native multimodal [6] |

The full report provides the detailed layer configuration, attention dimensions, expert routing, MTP decoding, and the distinction between flagship GLM‑5.3 and GLM‑5.3‑Flash.
